guidance: Geometry and a friction estimate, not a gearbox rating. The friction coefficient is an assumption you supply; check the wheel material, lubrication, power and thermal rating, and the manufacturer's data, before building or loading the drive.
method: Treats a cylindrical worm and wheel with no profile shift. Inputs are the module m in millimetres, the number of worm starts z1 (1 to 4), the wheel tooth count z2 (8 to 400), the worm pitch diameter d1 (1 to 2000 mm), the worm speed n1 (0 to 60000 rpm), the coefficient of friction mu (0.01 to 0.5) and the normal pressure angle (14.5, 20 or 25 degrees). The worm diameter factor is q = d1/m, the wheel pitch diameter d2 = m z2, the centre distance a = (d1 + d2)/2, the lead L = pi m z1 and the lead angle gamma = atan(z1 m / d1). The wheel turns at n2 = n1 z1 / z2; the worm pitch-line speed is v1 = pi d1 n1 and the sliding velocity is vs = v1 / cos gamma. The friction angle is phi = atan mu, and the drive is reported as self-locking when gamma is at or below phi, because the wheel then cannot drive the worm. Efficiency is the standard estimate eta = (cos alpha_n - mu tan gamma) / (cos alpha_n + mu cot gamma), clamped to 0-100 percent, where alpha_n is the normal pressure angle; it is a friction estimate, not a gearbox rating. Tip diameters are the unshifted d1 + 2m and d2 + 2m. Values are rounded for display to three decimals, and q and efficiency to two. A warning is shown when q falls outside 5-20 or the lead angle exceeds 25 degrees. Everything is computed in the browser; nothing is stored, uploaded or fetched.

sources.title: Worm gears (RoyMech): the lead angle atan(z1/q) with q = d1/m, the wheel pitch diameter from the axial pitch, the centre distance, the sliding velocity, the efficiency estimate (cos alpha_n - mu tan gamma)/(cos alpha_n + mu cot gamma) and the self-locking limit gamma = atan mu
